title: Pignoli Cookies
headnote: From an email Alexandra Audino Ferrari sent Linda in January 2015. Linda added her own notes by hand: bake 15 minutes, use sprayed parchment, and it makes 24.

items.raw: ¼ cup (35 g) pine nuts, or more to cover the tops

steps.text: Heat the oven to 325°F. Line cookie sheets with parchment and spray it.
Use a pastry cutter or food processor to break the almond paste down to a coarse, granulated texture. Put it in a mixing bowl and gradually work in the sugar.
In a separate clean bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff.
Fold the whites gently into the almond paste mixture.
Drop spoonfuls onto the sheets, about 2 inches apart. Press pine nuts into the tops — you want them covered.
Bake about 15 minutes, until lightly golden at the edges.
Let them cool a bit on the pan, then slide the whole sheet of parchment onto wire racks. Peel the cookies off once they are completely cool.

notes.label: Baking time
notes.text: the email said 10 to 12 minutes, and Alex added, “I also recall having to bake them a little longer, but that could be my oven.” Linda settled on 15.

notes.label: Pine nuts
notes.text: ¼ cup covers the tops only sparingly. Most bakery versions use about 1 cup for a batch this size; use as many as it takes.

notes.label: Almond paste, not marzipan
notes.text: marzipan has much more sugar and the cookies spread flat.

notes.label: Storage
notes.text: airtight at room temperature for a week, or frozen for 3 months.

openQuestion: Who is Alex to the family, and when do these get made — a Christmas cookie tray?
